Derived clarifications found and accepted as entailed: "write-offs (of every reason)" (compute sums every `adas_no_charge`); "Where the vehicle has no delivered network insurance claim repair on record, the window is taken as 99999 days, and the share is 0.20" (`no_record_days` in compute, "otherwise" tier); the tool sections (task_tools.py docstrings).

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.** Every atom of the two extended policies (rules, overwrites, prerequisite, baselines, all nine factor ladders, tool contracts) and of the referenced base policies has a faithful home; the retired surface is borne and marked retired; no claim without source.

Policy-side notes (do not change this verdict):
1. `adas_ext_alignment_comeback_credit.rule` books the credit "on the day that charge posts" while its tool books "dated today"; in this world the correction charge posted 2026-09-14 and the GT books the credit 2026-10-06. The source does not say what follows when that day has passed; the KB carries the clause as the source has it.
2. The retired base clause "An in-house calibration posts a calibration charge of calibration_price_usd" applied to every payer, while its replacement covers only accepted customer-pay calibrations; for insurance-claim and glass-program in-house calibrations no in-force charge basis remains in the source (the KB mirrors this: `calibration_charges_and_claim_transfers_288907a7` rule 2 retired, sublet and transfer rules in force). Outside this task's numbers.

## dependency_form

- Prerequisite sentence: verbatim, once, in the blocked policy's hub (`calibration_acceptance_payment_9b6f6d44`), plus one same-form restatement in the same doc; state form kept; no performer, action, tool or document named beside it. Not in any comeback-credit doc (the depended-on side does not disclose who waits on it).
- Tool names: each of the four ADAS task tools occurs only in its own hub's invocation block (kb lines: comeback tool 118–122 only in its hub; acceptance tool 227–231 only in its hub; the other two likewise).
- No dependency table, checklist, roadmap, ordered cross-problem step list, wrong-vs-right contrast or chain-walking example in any doc.
- Titles: "Customer Acceptance of a Customer-Pay Calibration" (the on_request type), "Comeback Credit on Alignment Corrections After a Network Claim Repair" (general subject), factor and baseline titles name general subjects; none mirrors this task (no customer-request + structural-repair + no-show situation in any title or opening).
- Baseline docs give no hint of modification (no "unless", "adjustments may apply", pointer or exception list); the comeback baseline names its own default constants ("a window share of 0.20 and a repair-class weight of 0.60") exactly as the source baseline rule does.
- Factor docs state ladders as rules, name no computation doc or sibling factor, say nothing about which tier customers usually fall on, and carry no task evidence rows. Each is reachable from the words of the records it reads (order source "customer request"; Insurance Claim Repairs class/delivered date; Workmanship Warranties name/status/issued date; Repair Estimates & Appointments no-show/closed date; check number 1 out of spec and corrected).
- Hop marks from the blind answer: the single hop was **state-derived**; nothing pre-solved.

**Verdict: PASS** (no KB-EXPLICIT RED).
